eventMetadata.context_description: The southwest monsoon (habagat) currently dominating Luzon supplies persistent cloud cover, scattered thunderstorms, and high humidity that limit daytime solar insolation and promote evaporative cooling, anchoring Manila’s maximum temperatures near the 30–32 °C range. Official PAGASA guidance and ensemble forecasts issued 12–13 August project a 29–31 °C high for 14 August under partly cloudy to overcast skies with moderate rain chances, consistent with August climatology of 30–31 °C peaks. These conditions explain why market-implied probabilities concentrate on 31 °C (39 %) and 32 °C (29 %), with only modest tail risk for brief clearing that could allow brief excursions above 33 °C. Fresh model runs and PAGASA updates over the next 24 hours will further refine resolution odds ahead of the daily maximum reading.

Historical analogs for mid-August under similar 500 mb patterns show peak readings clustering in the mid-70s, reinforcing trader consensus. Updated model runs expected this evening from the NHC and local NWS office will provide the final data ahead of market resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service and numerical model guidance converge on a San Francisco high of 66–69 °F for August 14, consistent with the marine-layer regime that typically limits afternoon warming along the immediate coast. Persistent onshore flow, cold-water upwelling, and morning stratus keep temperatures from rising much above the seasonal 67 °F average, while variable afternoon clearing can add a few degrees depending on the strength of the westerlies. Current forecasts show no significant offshore flow or heat-wave setup that would push readings into the low 70s, leaving the 68–69 °F bin with the highest market-implied probability. Updated model runs and the morning forecast discussion tomorrow will provide the final inputs for resolution at the official San Francisco station.

Upcoming IMD updates and refined numerical weather prediction runs over the next 24–48 hours will be the key near-term catalysts, with any shift in rainfall timing or intensity able to nudge the recorded maximum by 1–2°C at the official station.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts for Guangzhou point to scattered thunderstorms and showers on August 15, 2026, which are expected to moderate peak heating and keep the daily maximum near 34–35 °C. In this subtropical monsoon climate, August afternoon convection often develops under high humidity and weak steering flow, capping surface temperatures even as solar insolation remains strong. Historical August averages hover around 33 °C, with occasional spikes above 36 °C only when clearer, drier air masses arrive. Current model consensus favors the lower end of that range because of persistent moisture and cloud cover, though small shifts in timing or intensity of rain could still allow brief clearing and a higher reading. Traders are therefore clustering probability on 34–36 °C outcomes, reflecting the narrow window between typical convective cooling and the possibility of localized suppression of showers.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 15 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/ph/manila/RPLL.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Active southwest monsoon (habagat) patterns, including enhanced moisture and convective activity, are the primary driver moderating Manila's temperatures ahead of August 15. PAGASA's extended outlook projects a 26–33°C range for the day with high rain probability, consistent with typical wet-season conditions that increase cloud cover and reduce solar heating. Recent monitoring of Tropical Storm Nangka outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility and ongoing monsoon trough influences add uncertainty around exact rainfall timing and intensity, which directly affects daytime maxima. Trader positioning—led by 32°C (40.5%) and 31°C (35%)—aligns with expectations that persistent clouds and showers will likely cap peaks near or below the forecast midpoint rather than allowing clearer conditions to push toward 33°C or higher. Updated PAGASA model runs and daily bulletins through the weekend will provide key refinements on these variables.
